root_cause.text: In `vsock_update_buffer_size()`, clamping the buffer size to the maximum before clamping to the minimum allows the buffer size to exceed the configured maximum when the user sets a minimum larger than the maximum, violating the intended socket memory boundaries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reverses the order of bounds checks: originally `val > buffer_max_size` was checked first, then `val < buffer_min_size`; the fix checks the minimum first and then the maximum. The commit message explicitly states: "If a user sets a minimum buffer size larger than the maximum, the minimum check overrides the maximum check, inverting the constraint. This breaks the intended socket memory boundaries by allowing the vsk->buffer_size to grow beyond the configured vsk->buffer_max_size."

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder bounds checks to apply lower bound first, then upper bound, ensuring buffer size does not exceed maximum even if minimum is invalidly set above maximum.
intent_record.what: Swapped the order of the two bounds checks in vsock_update_buffer_size: first checks val < buffer_min_size and clamps to min, then checks val > buffer_max_size and clamps to max.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the clamping order changes from (max-then-min) to (min-then-max). For valid configurations (min <= max), the result is identical. For invalid configurations (min > max), the new order caps the value at max instead of raising it to min, preventing the final value from exceeding the maximum allowed size.
